messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: elevated model-load failures in us-west-2. error rate spike on model-service tier, initial failures: 8%
priya: ack. on-call here. looking now. paging alex/jordan.
alex: on it. can someone paste the warmup job logs?
jordan: pasting snippet from the node that failed:
```
[2026-03-17T02:14:11Z] model-loader: deserialization failed: invalid checksum for shard 12
[2026-03-17T02:14:11Z] compile: timeout while compiling kernels (120s)
[2026-03-17T02:14:12Z] runtime: OOM during initial KV cache allocate
containerd: container exit status 137
```
priya: hmm, deserial + compile timeout + OOM sequence. looks like a cold-warmup stampede on that node.
maya: visible customer impact: about 12 customers reported elevated 503s, top impacted tenant id=acct-91, requests failing at model-init path. Rolling window 3m error rate 8-10%.
alex: I can repro locally against shard 12 artifact. deserial seems to choke on the artifact size + concurrent warmups. propose: 1) throttle warmup concurrency on node 2) route new traffic to model-variant smaller-quantized v2-lite 2) evacuate problematic instance.
priya: agree. sam_runtime, can you push a policy to limit parallel warmup to 2 per GPU?
sam_runtime: deploying runtime flag: `--max-warmup-concurrency=2` to us-west-2 pool. Applying to pool-id: rw-usw2-pool-b.
sam_runtime: flag applied, draining in-progress warmups, starting fallback routing rule: if init fails -> route to model:v2-lite, ttl 10m.
jordan: also enabling compile timeout backoff: set `COMPILE_TIMEOUT=60s` for warmup jobs to reduce kernel compile burst.
priya: starting node remediation: cordon node ip 10.12.4.22 and rebooting to clear fragmented GPU memory.
maya: support note drafted for affected tenants: short blurb and ETA ~15-25m for rollback if successful. adding acct-91 to high-touch list.
alex: quick diagnostic - artifact checksum mismatch seen on one shard; re-pulled artifact on node shows different checksum than registry. grabbing `sha256` from S3 and local.
jordan: also found noisy GC on that node's docker overlay; may explain corrupt reads. adding `fsync` on artifact writes as mitigation.
priya: on-call handoff in 20m to alex once node remediation finishes. will keep monitoring.
incident-bot: incident severity -> SEV3 -> notifying oncall rotation per policy.
maya: customers notified via status page, incident link: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/3388889999 (draft published) :thumbsup:
alex: after node reboot, warmups stabilized on the node, no more checksum mismatch. routing rule still active for 30m. metrics: failed inits dropped from 8%->0.6% over 12 minutes.
priya: good. I'll update postmortem template with actions: artifact integrity check on pull, warmup concurrency cap, compile timeout backoff, fsync artifact writes, improved monitoring for checksum mismatch.
jordan: leaving a follow-up ticket: TKT-6123 "artifact read integrity - investigate overlayfs corner cases".
priya: handing oncall to alex now — please keep channel updated. handing_off -> alex :white_check_mark:
alex: thanks, taking over. will run the full blameless postmortem after stabilization.
priya: thanks all. closing active mitigation. reaction :rocket:
